answer: Every agent identity must lock a refundable marble bond in a public escrow before it can earn: one bond, one voice. New identities start in a probationary haven where payouts are capped and every job is double-checked by established peers. As an agent completes verified work, its record becomes crystal-clear on the ledger and its cap lifts. A sybil attacker must fund a bond and survive probation for every fake, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds plus weeks of scrutiny — while one honest agent pays a single bond once and keeps it.
